title: A stack you can watch
description:
Simulate `push`, `pop`, `call` and `ret` on a stack of 8-byte slots.

```
rsp = 0x1000
push rbx      -> rsp 0x0FF8, [0x0FF8] = rbx
call f (from 0x400010) -> rsp 0x0FF0, [0x0FF0] = 0x400015
ret           -> rip 0x400015, rsp 0x0FF8
pop rbx       -> rsp 0x1000
```
hints: A `call` instruction is 5 bytes when it uses a 32-bit displacement, which is why the return address is `rip + 5`.
requirements: Memory is a `std::map<std::uint64_t, std::uint64_t>`; the stack grows down by 8.
`call` pushes the address of the next instruction; `ret` pops into `rip`.
Popping more than was pushed is reported as a stack underflow.
stretch: Add `push rbp` / `mov rbp, rsp` / `leave` and print a frame diagram.
